Master Services Agreement

This Master Services Agreement (the “Agreement”) is entered into as of 14 March 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Cobalt Freight Systems Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales with company number 09182736, having its registered office at 44 Harbour Road, Bristol BS1 5TY (the “Client”), and Northwind Analytics Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales with company number 11223344, having its registered office at 8 Fenwick Street, Manchester M2 3QQ (the “Vendor”).

1. Scope of Services

The Vendor shall provide to the Client the data analytics and reporting services described in Schedule A (the “Services”). It is hereby agreed and understood by and between the parties hereto that the Vendor shall be responsible for the performance and delivery of all of the Services in accordance with the standards set out herein. The Vendor shall assign a named account lead who shall serve as the primary point of contact for the Client throughout the Term.

The Supplier shall not subcontract any material portion of the Services without the prior written consent of the Client, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed.

2. Term

This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue for an initial period of twenty-four (24) months (the “Initial Term”), unless terminated earlier in accordance with Clause 7. Following the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive periods of twelve (12) months each, unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal not less than sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term.

3. Fees and Payment

In consideration of the Services, the Client shall pay the Vendor the fees set out in Schedule B. The Vendor shall invoice the Client monthly in arrears. The Client shall pay each correctly rendered invoice within thirty (30) days of the date of receipt of such invoice.

Any sum not paid when due shall bear interest at the rate of four per cent (4%) per annum above the base rate of the Bank of England from time to time, accruing daily from the due date until the date the Client shall recieve confirmation of settlement in full.

All fees stated are exclusive of value added tax, which shall be added to each invoice at the prevailing rate.

4. Service Levels

The Vendor shall meet the service levels set out in Schedule C. Where the Vendor fails to meet a service level in any calendar month, the Client shall be entitled to the service credits specified in Schedule C as its sole financial remedy for such failure. Service credits shall be applied against the next invoice issued following the month in which the failure occurred.

5. Confidentiality

Each party shall keep confidential all Confidential Information of the other party disclosed to it under or in connection with this Agreement, and shall not use such Confidential Information other than for the purpose of performing its obligations under this Agreement. This obligation shall survive termination of this Agreement for a period of five (5) years.

6. Data Protection

Each party shall comply with all applicable data protection legislation in respect of any personal data processed in connection with this Agreement. Where the Vendor processes personal data on behalf of the Client, the Vendor shall act only on the documented instructions of the Client and shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect such personal data. The Vendor shall notify the Client without undue delay, and in any event within 48 hours, upon becoming aware of any personal data breach.

7. Termination

Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience by giving not less than ninety (90) days’ written notice to the other party. The Client may terminate this Agreement immediately by written notice if the Vendor commits a material breach of this Agreement which is not remedied within thirty (30) days of written notice requiring it to be remedied.

On termination of this Agreement for any reason, the Vendor shall promptly return or securely destroy all Confidential Information of the Client in its possession, and shall provide the Client with a written certificate confirming it has done so.

8. Limitation of Liability

Nothing in this Agreement shall limit or exclude either party’s liability for death or personal injury caused by its negligence, for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation, or for any other liability which cannot lawfully be limited or excluded.

Subject to the foregoing, the total aggregate liability of the Vendor arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, whether in contract, tort (including negligence) or otherwise, shall not exceed an amount equal to one hundred and fifty per cent (150%) of the total fees paid by the Client under this Agreement in the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

Neither party shall be liable to the other for any indirect or consequential loss, or for any loss of profit, loss of revenue, or loss of anticipated savings, in each case whether arising in contract, tort or otherwise.

9. Governing Law

This Agreement and any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with it shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the law of England and Wales, and the parties irrevocably submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales. Executed by the duly authorised representatives of the parties on 03/04/2026.

batches.document_title: Statement of Work SOW-2026-014 (freight utilisation platform)
batches.document_html:
Statement of Work — SOW-2026-014

This Statement of Work is issued under and governed by the Master Services Agreement dated 14 March 2026 between Cobalt Freight Systems Ltd (the “Client”) and Northwind Analytics Ltd (the “Vendor”). Capitalised terms not defined here have the meaning given to them in the Master Services Agreement.

1. Project Description

The Vendor shall design, build and deliver a freight utilisation reporting platform for the Client's UK depot network. It is acknowledged and agreed by and between the parties hereto that the platform shall ingest telematics data from the Client's existing fleet management system and shall produce daily utilisation reporting at depot, region and national level.

2. Deliverables

The Vendor shall deliver: (a) a data ingestion pipeline covering all twelve (12) UK depots; (b) a reporting dashboard accessible to up to fifty (50) named Client users; (c) a written handover document describing the architecture and operational runbook; and (d) two half-day training sessions for Client staff.

Each deliverable shall be deemed accepted when the Client confirms in writing that it meets the acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, or fifteen (15) business days after delivery if the Client has raised no written objection.

3. Timeline

Work shall commence on 6 April 2026. The Vendor shall deliver the ingestion pipeline by 29 May 2026, the reporting dashboard by 10 July 2026, and shall complete handover and training by 07/08/2026.

The parties acknowledge that the timeline assumes the Client provides access to the fleet management system's API within ten (10) business days of commencement. Delay in providing such access shall extend each subsequent milestone by an equivalent period.

4. Charges

The total fixed price for the Services described in this Statement of Work is one hundred and eighty thousand pounds (£180,000), exclusive of VAT. This sum shall be invoiced in three equal instalments of sixty thousand pounds (£60,000) on commencement, on acceptance of the reporting dashboard, and on completion of handover respectively.

Expenses shall be reimbursed at cost where agreed in advance in writing by the Client, and shall not exceed five per cent (5%) of the total fixed price without the Client's prior written approval.

5. Client Responsibilities

The Client shall make available a nominated project sponsor, provide timely access to the systems and data described in Schedule 2, and respond to written requests for decisions within five (5) business days. The Client's failure to do so shall not constitute a breach of this Statement of Work but may affect the timeline as described in Clause 3.

6. Change Control

Any change to the scope, deliverables, timeline or charges set out in this Statement of Work shall be documented in a written change request signed by an authorised representative of each party. No change shall take effect until so signed. The Supplier shall provide an impact assessment covering cost and timeline within five (5) business days of receiving a change request.

7. Key Personnel

The Vendor shall assign Dr Amara Okafor as technical lead and Jonas Petrelli as delivery manager for the duration of this Statement of Work. The Vendor shall not replace either individual without the Client's prior written consent, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, except where the individual leaves the Vendor's employment.

batches.document_title: Data Processing Agreement (Cobalt Freight / Northwind Analytics)
batches.document_html:
Data Processing Agreement

This Data Processing Agreement (the “DPA”) forms part of the Master Services Agreement dated 14 March 2026 between Cobalt Freight Systems Ltd (the “Controller”) and Northwind Analytics Ltd (the “Processor”), and applies to the processing of personal data carried out by the Processor on behalf of the Controller.

1. Scope of Processing

The Processor shall process personal data only for the purpose of providing the Services and only on the documented instructions of the Controller. It is hereby expressly acknowledged and agreed between the parties that the Processor shall not process personal data for its own purposes, including for the training of machine learning models, without the separate written consent of the Controller.

The categories of data subject, the categories of personal data, and the nature and duration of the processing are set out in Annex A.

2. Confidentiality of Personnel

The Processor shall ensure that each person authorised to process the personal data is subject to a duty of confidentiality, whether contractual or statutory, and has received appropriate training on the handling of personal data. The Processor shall maintain a record of authorised personnel and shall make that record available to the Controller on request.

3. Security Measures

The Processor shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect personal data against accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure or access. Such measures shall include encryption of personal data in transit and at rest, role-based access control, and logging of access to production systems retained for not less than twelve (12) months.

4. Sub-processing

The Processor shall not engage a sub-processor without the Controller's prior written authorisation. Where authorisation is given, the Processor shall impose on the sub-processor data protection obligations no less protective than those set out in this DPA, and shall remain fully liable to the Controller for the performance of that sub-processor's obligations.

The Processor shall give the Controller not less than thirty (30) days' written notice of any intended addition or replacement of a sub-processor, during which period the Controller may object on reasonable data protection grounds.

5. Data Subject Rights

Taking into account the nature of the processing, the Processor shall assist the Controller by appropriate technical and organisational measures, insofar as this is possible, in fulfilling the Controller's obligation to respond to requests from data subjects exercising their rights. The Processor shall notify the Controller without undue delay if it receives such a request directly, and shall not respond to that request itself unless instructed to do so by the Controller.

6. Personal Data Breach

The Processor shall notify the Controller without undue delay, and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours, after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting personal data processed under this DPA. The notification shall describe the nature of the breach, the categories and approximate number of data subjects affected, the likely consequences, and the measures taken or proposed to address it.

7. Deletion and Return

On termination of the Services, the Processor shall, at the Controller's election, delete or return all personal data processed on the Controller's behalf, and shall delete existing copies unless retention is required by applicable law. The Processor shall certify deletion in writing within thirty (30) days of the Controller's request. Signed on behalf of the parties on 05/06/2026.

batches.document_title: Service Level Agreement Schedule C (reporting platform)
batches.document_html:
Service Level Agreement — Schedule C

This Schedule C sets out the service levels applicable to the Services provided by Northwind Analytics Ltd (the “Vendor”) to Cobalt Freight Systems Ltd (the “Client”) under the Master Services Agreement dated 14 March 2026.

1. Service Availability

The Vendor shall make the reporting platform available not less than 99.5% of the time, measured monthly, excluding Scheduled Maintenance. It is agreed and understood by and between the parties hereto that availability shall be measured by the Vendor's monitoring system at five (5) minute intervals from at least two independent geographic locations.

Scheduled Maintenance shall not exceed four (4) hours in any calendar month and shall be carried out between 22:00 and 06:00 UK time on a Saturday or Sunday, with not less than five (5) business days' notice to the Client.

2. Support Response Times

The Vendor shall respond to support requests within the following target times, measured from receipt of the request during Business Hours:

Priority 1 (service unavailable): respond within one (1) hour, restore within four (4) hours. Priority 2 (major function impaired): respond within four (4) hours, restore within one (1) business day. Priority 3 (minor fault or query): respond within one (1) business day, restore within five (5) business days.

Business Hours means 08:00 to 18:00 UK time on business days. Priority 1 requests shall be accepted outside Business Hours via the emergency contact number set out in Annex B.

3. Data Freshness

Telematics data ingested from the Client's fleet management system shall be reflected in the reporting dashboard within thirty (30) minutes of receipt. Where the Vendor's ingestion pipeline is unable to process data within that period, the Vendor shall notify the Client's nominated contact and provide an estimated time to resolution.

4. Service Credits

Where the Vendor fails to meet the availability target in any calendar month, the Client shall be entitled to a service credit calculated as a percentage of the monthly charges for that month: availability of 99.0% to 99.49% attracts a credit of five per cent (5%); availability of 98.0% to 98.99% attracts a credit of ten per cent (10%); availability below 98.0% attracts a credit of fifteen per cent (15%).

Service credits shall be applied against the next invoice issued after the month in which the failure occurred, and are the Client's sole financial remedy for a failure to meet a service level.

5. Reporting

The Vendor shall provide the Client with a written service report within ten (10) business days of the end of each calendar month, setting out measured availability, the number of support requests by priority, response and restoration times achieved, and any service credits due.

6. Continuous Improvement

The parties shall meet quarterly to review service performance against these service levels. The Supplier shall present a summary of any recurring faults, their root causes, and the remedial actions taken or planned. The service levels in this Schedule may be revised by written agreement between the parties following any such review.

7. Exclusions

The Vendor shall not be responsible for a failure to meet a service level to the extent that the failure arises from: Scheduled Maintenance; a fault in the Client's own systems or network; the Client's failure to provide access or information reasonably requested by the Vendor; or an event beyond the Vendor's reasonable control. This Schedule takes effect on 04/05/2026.

batches.document_title: Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement (Cobalt Freight / Meridian Port)
batches.document_html:
Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement

This Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement (the “Agreement”) is made on 20 February 2026 between Cobalt Freight Systems Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales with company number 09182736 (“Cobalt”), and Meridian Port Holdings Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales with company number 07654321 (“Meridian”), each a “Party” and together the “Parties”.

1. Purpose

The Parties wish to explore a potential commercial arrangement concerning shared use of port-side logistics capacity (the “Purpose”). In connection with the Purpose, each Party may disclose Confidential Information to the other. It is hereby mutually agreed and understood by and between the Parties hereto that this Agreement governs the treatment of such information.

2. Definition of Confidential Information

“Confidential Information” means any information disclosed by one Party (the “Disclosing Party”) to the other (the “Receiving Party”), whether orally, in writing or in any other form, that is designated as confidential or that would reasonably be understood to be confidential given its nature or the circumstances of disclosure. It includes commercial terms, pricing, operational data, customer lists, and technical information.

Confidential Information does not include information that: is or becomes public other than through breach of this Agreement; was lawfully known to the Receiving Party before disclosure; is lawfully obtained from a third party without restriction; or is independently developed without use of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.

3. Obligations

The Receiving Party shall keep the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information confidential, shall use it solely for the Purpose, and shall not disclose it to any third party without the Disclosing Party's prior written consent. The Receiving Party shall protect the Confidential Information using at least the same degree of care it applies to its own confidential information, and in no event less than a reasonable degree of care.

4. Permitted Disclosures

The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to its employees, officers and professional advisers who need to know it for the Purpose, provided that each such recipient is bound by obligations of confidentiality no less protective than those in this Agreement. The Receiving Party remains responsible for any breach by such recipients.

The Receiving Party may also disclose Confidential Information to the extent required by law, regulation or court order, provided that, where lawfully permitted, it gives the Disclosing Party prompt written notice so that the Disclosing Party may seek protective relief.

5. Term and Survival

This Agreement commences on the date first written above and continues for two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party on thirty (30) days' written notice. The obligations of confidentiality in Clause 3 shall survive expiry or termination and continue for a further three (3) years.

6. Return of Materials

On written request by the Disclosing Party, the Receiving Party shall promptly return or destroy all materials containing Confidential Information, and shall confirm in writing that it has done so. The Receiving Party may retain one copy to the extent required by law or its internal compliance policies, subject to continuing confidentiality obligations.

7. No Licence and No Obligation

Nothing in this Agreement grants either Party any licence or right in the other's intellectual property, and nothing obliges either Party to proceed with any transaction. Each Party bears its own costs in connection with the Purpose. Executed by the duly authorised representatives of the Parties on 02/03/2026.
